chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who wants to go ahead in it, for which there is no time earlier than it. He said: “When the sun passes the meridian.”

And about one who wishes to remain behind in Makkah on the eve of al-Tarwiyah—until what hour is it permissible for him to remain behind? He said: “That is broader for him, until he reaches Minā by morning.”

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passed the meridian; noon time began
key_terms.عَشِيَّةَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eve of the Day of Tarwiyah
key_terms.يَتَقَدَّمَ: to go ahead or depart earlier

ai.seo_question: When may a pilgrim leave for Minā, and how late may he remain in Makkah before the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal timing for departing to Minā during hajj. It states that one who wishes to go earlier may do so from the time of zawāl, while one who delays staying in Makkah on the eve of al-Tarwiyah has leeway until he arrives in Minā by morning.
